Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T06:18:28Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for frontend-proxy is driven by HTTP 504s on POST /api/checkout, not by a failure of frontend-proxy itself: Envoy's ingress logs and spans show '504 UT response_timeout' at exactly 15000 ms against the 'frontend' upstream (facts: 7984acc6-f949-4a99-afa8-15550e5d1467-t0:79280e6b-622e-4b13-b755-6f04153fe994, cf6b30b8-9120-4100-9c2e-972925bc360f-t0:6527a2f0-dfce-40cb-b217-68b7f755dfe0). Inside that path, checkout's Kafka publish span 'orders publish' consumed 19.24 s of a 19.34 s PlaceOrder while cart, payment, currency, product-catalog, shipping, email and quote calls finished in milliseconds (fact: 90de1862-649b-4122-9f0c-ebee551b8d84-t0:10e5a3c3-2817-4b1f-ba92-bae0905f353b). That publish span does not appear among the longest pre-incident checkout spans (all <= 2.34 ms; PlaceOrder max 168.7 ms at 06:13:56), and appears at 15.2-19.2 s after the Kafka pod was replaced (facts: c9fcf7bf-fab7-4581-ba93-34617b699df1-t0:2b9bacf4-fcd4-4c30-b9cf-77cc640ed812, c0d3a195-c5c4-4bd0-9bcc-b2275f38e345-t0:7909641a-3988-494c-b519-086af32afbc0). During the window Deployment kafka's pod template was changed (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:15:57Z, generation 2, new ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485, old pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 deleted); the fresh broker was unreachable from checkout until 06:17:42Z and was CPU-throttled at ~99% of CFS periods right after start. frontend-proxy ingress error-span completions rose from 0-4 per 2-minute bucket (05:54-06:18) to ~16-36 per bucket from 06:19:00 through 06:29:00. The restart is the only object-level change observed at the onset, but the broker was already idle (~0.02 cores, ~1% throttling) while publish spans were still 15-19 s at 06:26:47, so the persistence is not fully explained; the enabled fault flag kafkaQueueProblems='on' in ConfigMap flagd-config (declared effect: overloading the Kafka queue and causing a lag spike) remains a strong hypothesis that could not be timed or measured. Conclusion is partial: the failure path and the implicated change are evidenced, the broker-side mechanism is not. Telemetry ends around 06:27-06:29Z, so whether the condition persisted afterwards is unknown.

claims.text: frontend-proxy carries ERROR-status span counts (1280 cumulative STATUS_CODE_ERROR vs 57115 STATUS_CODE_UNSET at 06:31:08), and its ingress error-span completions rose from 0-4 per 2-minute window across 05:54:00-06:18:00 to 30.3, 22.7, 25.3, 16, 32, 33.3, 19.6, 30.7, 21.3, 36 and 28.7 per 2-minute window from 06:19:00 through 06:29:00.

The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504 on the 'ingress' operation with duration ~15.0 s (status_tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR), and pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bh295 logs repeated lines '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000 ... frontend', while other routes such as 'GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO' returned 200 via_upstream in 36 ms.

In trace 27a9320f744d8508200595d85ed32e34 the checkout span 'orders publish' (Kafka publish to topic orders) lasted 19.238 s of a 19.339 s oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, while cart POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart was 0.338 ms, payment charge 0.352 ms, currency Convert 0.626 ms, shipping POST quote 2.027 ms and email send_email 2.951 ms; frontend 'POST /api/checkout' completed with http.status_code 200 after 19.342 s while the frontend-proxy ingress span for the same trace was cut at 15.000 s with 504.

Kafka publish latency is the only part of the checkout path that changed: in the pre-change checkout span slice (spans starting 06:13:56-06:13:59Z) the longest checkout spans were PlaceOrder 168.7 ms, 88.8 ms and 56.8 ms and no 'orders publish' span appears among the 14 longest spans (all <= 2.34 ms), whereas in the post-change slice (spans starting 06:26:47Z) 'orders publish' spans of 19.238 s, 17.261 s and 15.238 s appear under PlaceOrder spans of 19.339 s, 17.370 s and 15.440 s.

Deployment kafka in namespace otel-demo is at deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2 and generation 2 with pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:15:57Z; its condition NewReplicaSetAvailable names ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485, and pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 (owner ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485) started 2026-11-17T06:15:57Z with container startedAt 06:15:58Z and restartCount 0, while every other otel-demo pod started at 05:42:52-05:44:38Z.

Events in namespace otel-demo during the window include one ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate and one ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete, two Pod Created, one Pod Killing and two Pod Started, consistent with the kafka ReplicaSet replacement recorded by the pod and Deployment state.

checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-6qppz logged 'dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused', 'Failed to write message: kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to', and 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open' between 06:17:06Z and 06:17:39Z, then 'Connected to broker at kafka:9092 (registered as #1)' and 'producer/leader/orders/0 selected broker 1' at 06:17:42Z.

The new broker container kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 was heavily CPU-throttled right after start: throttled-periods/periods ratio 0.993 (06:17), 0.882 (06:18), 0.626 (06:19), 0.449 (06:20), 0.350, 0.103, then ~0.012 from 06:23 onward, against ~0.008-0.021 for the previous pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2; its CPU usage peaked at 0.348 cores (06:18) and settled near 0.02 cores.

The restarted broker's log shows it replaying PartitionRecords for topics including orders (06:17:35Z) and then '[Broker id=1] Leader orders-0 ... starts at leader epoch 0 from offset 0 ... high watermark 0, ISR [1]', followed by consumer-group rebalances for groups fraud-detection and accounting at 06:17:39-06:17:41Z; the readable error/warn/timeout lines for that container all fall in 06:17:33-06:17:41Z.

The Kafka container's memory working set grew from 2.4 MiB at pod start to ~254 MiB (06:17), ~555 MiB (06:18) and plateaued at ~593 MiB from 06:28 to 06:31 against a 900Mi limit, with container restartCount 0 and empty lastState (no OOMKill recorded on the new broker).

ConfigMap flagd-config (namespace otel-demo) contains an ENABLED flag 'kafkaQueueProblems' with defaultVariant 'on' (variant on=100) described as 'Overloads Kafka queue while simultaneously introducing a consumer side delay leading to a lag spike'; every other fault flag in the same file (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) is set to 'off'.
ConfigMap flagd-config was created at 2026-11-17T05:42:52Z and is annotated as part of the otel-demo Helm release; the checkout Deployment consumes flags through FLAGD_HOST=flagd / FLAGD_PORT=8013.

For the 06:20:00-06:31:08 window the query comparing nonzero ERROR-span increases per service and operation returned exactly two series: frontend-proxy span 'ingress' (171.2 per 10m) and recommendation span '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (1.08 per 10m).
Checkout PlaceOrder call rate was steady across the window (0.32-0.63 spans/s from 05:55 to 06:31, no upward step), so the error-rate rise is not explained by increased checkout traffic.

The sporadic frontend-proxy errors before the escalation were a different failure mode: 06:08:57Z-06:11:57Z ingress spans returned http.status_code 503 on GET paths (user_browse_product, user_get_ads) with durations of 19.8 ms to 858 ms, not 504s on POST /api/checkout.

Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm shows an independent container failure: lastState terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 finishedAt 2026-11-17T06:09:02Z, restartCount 2, container running and Ready again since 06:09:16Z.

The Deployment kafka pod-template change at 06:15:57Z is the trigger for the alert: it killed the only broker (checkout got connection refused 06:17:06-06:17:39Z), left the replacement broker heavily CPU-throttled until ~06:23, and after the replacement the checkout 'orders publish' span to topic orders rose from <=2.34 ms to 15.2-19.2 s, pushing frontend's POST /api/checkout past frontend-proxy/Envoy's 15 s response timeout so those requests are counted as frontend-proxy 504 errors.

The enabled fault-injection flag kafkaQueueProblems ('on', value 100) in ConfigMap flagd-config may be the deeper cause of the sustained Kafka publish latency: its declared effect (overloading the Kafka queue and causing a lag spike) matches the observed single slow stage ('orders publish'), and it is the only enabled fault flag in the file. This cannot be confirmed: broker-side produce latency and consumer lag are not scraped in this Prometheus and change history is not integrated, and it is counter-indicated by the observation that publishes were <=2.34 ms at 06:13:56 while the ConfigMap read now shows the flag 'on' with creation timestamp 05:42:52Z, before the incident.

Broker cold-start CPU throttling under the 400m CPU limit contributed to the 06:16-06:23 portion of the timeouts but does not by itself explain the sustained latency, because at 06:26:47Z the new broker was at ~0.02 cores with ~1% throttling while the checkout publish span was still 19.238 s.

A failing downstream service is not the explanation: in the sampled traces cart POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (0.338 ms), payment charge (0.352 ms), currency Convert (0.626 ms), product-catalog GetProduct (0.117 ms), shipping POST quote (2.027 ms) and email send_email (2.951 ms) all completed in milliseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, and the query for nonzero ERROR-span series in 06:20-06:30 returned only frontend-proxy ingress and recommendation's /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (1.08 per 10m).

frontend itself was not returning errors in the traced cases: its 'POST /api/checkout' span completed with http.status_code 200 after 19.34 s while frontend-proxy had already closed the same request at 15.000 s, so the 504 originates in the frontend-proxy/Envoy response timeout, not in a frontend error response.

The low-level pre-escalation frontend-proxy errors (503 on GET browse-product and get-ads between 06:08:57Z and 06:11:57Z, 19.8-858 ms) were considered as the signal behind this alert and rejected as its driver: they are a different status code and path set, they ended before 06:12, and the sustained escalation from 06:19:00 consists of 15 s HTTP 504s on POST /api/checkout.

Confirm whether flag kafkaQueueProblems in ConfigMap flagd-config was set to 'on' as a test injection and, if so, set it to 'off' and re-measure the checkout 'orders publish' span latency; this needs the change-history integration, which is not available in this Run.

Add Kafka broker-level telemetry (produce request latency, request-queue time, consumer-group lag) or broker DEBUG logging for produce handling; this Prometheus exposes no kafka_* series, so broker-side delay cannot currently be separated from client-side backlog.

Verify kafka's storage configuration and the reason for the rollout restart at 06:15:57Z: the restarted broker reported orders-0 starting 'from offset 0' with 'high watermark 0', which is consistent with the topic data not surviving the pod replacement and would need a PersistentVolume check plus the (unavailable) change history.

Handle the fraud-detection OOMKill separately (container memory behaviour and limits for pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm, exit code 137 at 06:09:02Z); it is not tied to the frontend-proxy 504 path in the evidence gathered here.

gaps: No change history is available (change_history integration is not integrated): who or what triggered the Deployment kafka rollout restart at 2026-11-17T06:15:57Z, and whether or when flag kafkaQueueProblems in ConfigMap flagd-config was set to 'on', cannot be established.

Telemetry ends before the end of the authorized window: metric samples stop around 06:29:00Z and traces around 06:27:07Z, and the instant query for frontend-proxy ingress ERROR increase over 06:28:08-06:31:08 returned no_data (evidence 9c36f0b5-c771-446b-8e3c-15333b066ca7-t2:72f18111-a1fe-49a7-a90d-fb58c2b69774), so whether the 504 rate was still elevated or recovering after 06:29 is unknown; no data is not zero.

flagd pod logs were not retrievable (query for flagd-f546d44c9-zx5qq returned no_data, evidence ee1ad07c-6ea8-437c-add2-d117b54fd223-t0:9702bc98-3b98-4940-977b-679e2443c9b4), so flag evaluation of kafkaQueueProblems by checkout at the time of the incident could not be verified.

Kafka storage was not verified: the Deployment and pod objects returned no volume information, so whether topic data survives broker restarts (emptyDir vs PersistentVolumeClaim) is unknown, even though the restarted broker reported orders-0 at offset 0 and high watermark 0.

Only representative samples were inspected: the checkout pre/post-change span slices are limited and truncated reads (c9fcf7bf-fab7-4581-ba93-34617b699df1-t0:2b9bacf4-fcd4-4c30-b9cf-77cc640ed812, c0d3a195-c5c4-4bd0-9bcc-b2275f38e345-t0:7909641a-3988-494c-b519-086af32afbc0), so downstream-service health statements rest on those sampled traces, not on complete request coverage.

Kafka pod logs after 06:26:30Z could not be read (query returned no_data, evidence 72fbd07f-5305-41fd-872e-3f52020359d8-t1:90e8a9fa-469e-45b7-92d2-358c90b5867f), so the broker's own activity during the final minutes of the window is unknown; so is the accounting consumer's behaviour (its filtered log query returned no_data, evidence ee1ad07c-6ea8-437c-add2-d117b54fd223-t1:08bd266f-b940-4061-bfe1-80ae120d90da).
next_steps: Retrieve change history for the otel-demo namespace around 06:00-06:20Z (Kafka rollout restart at 06:15:57Z, any flagd-config edits) once a change-history source is available.
Scrape Kafka broker JMX metrics (produce request latency, request queue time, consumer group lag) or enable broker DEBUG logging to quantify the broker-side component of the 15-19 s publish latency.
If kafkaQueueProblems is a test injection, disable it and watch the checkout 'orders publish' span and the frontend-proxy 504 rate to confirm or refute the hypothesis.
Verify kafka's volume configuration and whether the orders topic data was lost by the pod replacement.
Investigate the fraud-detection container OOMKill (exit 137) as a separate issue, and re-check whether frontend-proxy ingress 504s decayed after 06:29Z once fresh metrics are available.
